message.reasoning_content: We need to determine the crime(s) based on facts. The scenario: employee demands resignation and wages, boss refuses. Employee buys lighter, goes back, cuts LPG cylinder pipe, opens valve releasing gas, threatens boss to agree to resignation. Boss closes valve, takes him to kitchen to negotiate, they don't reach agreement, employee again takes lighter and tries to ignite near gas cylinder, boss stops and calls police. So the employee is threatening to cause explosion, possibly endangering public safety. The crime likely is "放火" (arson) or "非法点燃、放火罪". In Chinese criminal law, using gas to cause fire is arson. The act of cutting gas cylinder and threatening to ignite is dangerous. The crime could be "放火罪" (arson) under Article 114. In examples, similar scenario: Wu case with lighting bedding -> 放火. Also earlier example: "失火" for accidental fire. Here it's intentional. So "放火". Also maybe "敲诈勒索"? He is demanding resignation and wages, using threat of fire. Could be "敲诈勒索罪". But the main act is threatening to cause fire, not actual damage. The law: Threatening to set fire may be considered "敲诈勒索罪" if extortion. However typical classification: Using dangerous means to coerce is extortion. But the prosecution likely charges "放火罪". In examples, they used "放火" for similar. So answer: [罪名]放火<eoa>
